## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
Two new Webhook trigger options have been added that limit how a webhook can be used to trigger an automation. A new _allowed_methods_ option can be used to control which HTTP request methods can activate the trigger (GET, HEAD, POST, PUT).  And the _local_only_ option is used allow devices outside your local network to activate the trigger.

Previously all webhook triggers could be activated by HEAD, POST, and PUT methods from any device (local or on the internet). With the new options, only POST and PUT are enabled by default. 

**In Home Assistant version 2023.7.0 any webhook trigger that does not set _local_only_ to false can only be activated by devices on the same network as Home Assistant.**

To update your webhook triggers, click the gear/cog icon beside the Webhook ID. Then select an appropriate value for _Only accessible from the local network_. It is necessary to deselect the option for the 'Save' button to appear. Then reselect the option if it should be enabled. This will make the repair warning go away.

![Screenshot 2022-09-14 10 19 56 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/289218/190221194-c18f9ec8-5847-4358-aa69-eaf81f5518d1.png)

See the [webhook trigger documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/trigger/#webhook-trigger) for a description of the new options. And please review the new the [Webhook Security](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/trigger/#webhook-security) section for best practices when using webhook triggers.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR adds two new options for webhook triggers:
1. __allowed_methods__: Controls which methods can be used with a webhook trigger. Allowed methods include GET, HEAD, POST, and PUT. By default only POST and PUT are enabled. Methods that are not enabled will return 200 OK to the caller, but will not trigger the webhook; they will cause a log message to be generated though.
2. __local_only__: Controls whether the webhook trigger can be accessed by devices on the internet. A log message will be generated for access attempts from the internet when this option is enabled. This option is ignored for webhook triggers that are activated via Nabu Casa Cloud or via the websocket API.

See #56446 & #65928 for a discussion on the security implications of this change.

```yaml

  trigger:
    - platform: webhook
      webhook_id: "some_hook_id"
      allowed_methods:
        - POST
        - PUT
      local_only: true
```

This PR breaks the companion apps and automation that relies on external requests. It also will break some other integrations that either rely on external requests or on HEAD (I think at least Twillio used that to verify?)

We need to find a way to transition users to better defaults.

> This PR breaks the companion apps and automation that relies on external requests. It also will break some other integrations that either rely on external requests or on HEAD (I think at least Twillio used that to verify?)

I didn't anticipate this PR breaking integrations or companion apps. I had intended it to only be a breaking change for automations that contain webhook triggers. Could you give an example of a companion app or integration that would break with this change? I definitely don't want to do this, and will fix it if provided with an example to test with.

Note:
1. I haven't changed the default for `local_only` when calling `async_register`. It still defaults to `False`. I was anticipating that all integrations using webhooks would still use this default.
2. With this PR a HEAD request should still return 200 OK for all webhooks; even if HEAD isn't allowed or if the webhook is local_only. A website using a HEAD request to check to see if the URL is valid will still get a 200 OK response. The difference with this PR is that a HEAD request won't reach the webhook handler method within Home Assistant if HEAD isn't allowed.


> We need to find a way to transition users to better defaults.

I've been looking for a way to silently modify the automations that existed prior to this PR to set `local_only=False` for them. I don't think I have enough experience with Home Assistant to do this. Is there a way to upgrade automations.yaml when this PR runs the first time?

I'm okay with removing the changes related to `local_only` from this PR if that would be preferable too. Maybe trying to default this to True is just too much for now. I think it also implies that systems on the internet cannot trigger a webhook, and gives a false sense of security. In actuality, since CORS is enabled for /api/webhook/, any website on the internet can still trigger the webhook even when `local_only=True`.

issue_context.title: Webhooks missing support for GET requests
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Webhooks currently only support POST-style requests. This limits the use of this feature. While I'm sure there are dozens of other examples, the Shelly Button only supports GET requests for button actions.

It's probably reasonable to support POST requests for any webhook request that has a data payload.

But there's no good reason why a simple no-data webhook can't be triggered via a GET. It's not like there's security on a POST request...

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2021.12.10

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

n/a

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/automation/trigger/#webhook-trigger

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

There's a community feature request for GET support for webhooks that's been ignored (no comments from HA team) for almost two years. 

https://community.home-assistant.io/t/allow-get-requests-to-trigger-webhooks/106077

If there's a good reason why this can't be done, it would be worth commenting there, so that we can stop trying for it, and look for work-arounds.

If it's merely a matter of resources/priorities, then it would be worth saying _that,_ and let's see if it inspires a contribution.

Ohh! I think I might see what is happening. From your log, it looks like this PR was installed as a custom component. Is that correct? If that is the case all of the core/built-in components, like the mobile_app, will still be using the `async_register` method from the core/built-in webhook component and won't be calling the method inside the custom component.
